dedupe_keys.name: groundwater time series modelling challenge five well head series with meteorological inputs egu 2022 hess 2024

description: The Groundwater Time Series Modelling Challenge is an open benchmark of hydraulic head records from five monitoring wells, set up to compare statistical, conceptual and process-based groundwater models on equal terms. It was announced at the 2022 EGU General Assembly by R.A. Collenteur (Eawag), E. Haaf (Chalmers), T. Liesch and A. Wunsch (KIT) and M. Bakker (TU Delft), and its results were published in Hydrology and Earth System Sciences in 2024. Coverage: wells in sedimentary aquifers in Germany (a confined karst aquifer in Bavaria), the Netherlands, two in Sweden and one in the USA, each with daily head data split into calibration and testing periods and daily input series; for the German well these are E-OBS precipitation, temperature, pressure, humidity, wind, radiation and Makkink evaporation. Format and access: CSV files per site (heads, full heads and inputs) with a README describing each well, a locations table, all submitted results and the submission rules in a GitHub repository, now archived; free. Licence: GPL-3.0 (repository LICENSE file). Caveats: only five wells, each site has its own input variables (only the German README was read), and the repository is archived after publication so no new submissions are scored. Simulation uses: benchmarking groundwater level models that feed drought and supply capacity planning and climate adaptation of water supply wells. Related records: MODFLOW 6 (model-modflow-6) is the standard process-based groundwater model such benchmarks compare against.
